name: Seolleongtang
description: A milky soup of ox bones, brisket and other cuts, simmered for hours to a whole day. It is a local dish of Seoul, seasoned at the table.
how_to_eat: Add salt, pepper and spring onion yourself, then mix in rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'seolleongtang' at long-running soup restaurants in Seoul.

name: Tteokbokki
description: Chewy cylinder rice cakes simmered in spicy gochujang sauce, often with fish cakes, boiled eggs and scallions. The spicy version is credited to Ma Bok-rim in Sindang, Seoul, in 1953.
how_to_eat: Eat with a toothpick or fork from a paper cup or shared pan.
how_to_order: Buy a cup at street stalls (pojangmacha), or visit Sindang-dong's tteokbokki alley in Seoul.

name: Budae-jjigae
description: Spicy 'army base stew' of ham, sausage, Spam, kimchi, instant noodles, gochujang and American cheese, born from post-war scarcity. Uijeongbu in Gyeonggi claims to have first made it and has a street of budae-jjigae restaurants.
how_to_eat: Share the pot cooked at the table, with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'budae-jjigae' on Uijeongbu's Budae-jjigae Street or at chains across Korea.

name: Jjajangmyeon
description: Wheat noodles under a thick black-bean (chunjang) sauce with diced pork and vegetables, a Korean take on Chinese zhajiangmian. It developed among Shandong migrants in Incheon, and was served at Gonghwachun in Incheon Chinatown, founded in 1905.
how_to_eat: Mix the sauce through the noodles before eating, with pickled radish on the side.
how_to_order: Order from Korean-Chinese restaurants, or visit Incheon Chinatown.

name: Bulgogi
description: Thin, marinated slices of meat, most commonly beef, grilled on a barbecue or stove-top griddle. A delicacy of Pyongan that became popular in Seoul through refugees, it is very popular across South Korea, from upscale restaurants to supermarket kits.
how_to_eat: Wrap the meat in lettuce with garlic and ssamjang.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bulgogi' at Korean barbecue restaurants.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
description: Fried chicken dishes created in South Korea, either plain 'huraideu' or coated in spicy-sweet 'yangnyeom' sauce. It is eaten as a meal, an anju with drinks or an after-meal snack, and is famously paired with beer ('chimaek').
how_to_eat: Order half-and-half (plain and yangnyeom) and eat with pickled radish and beer.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chikin' at fried chicken shops, or order delivery.

name: Hotteok
description: A filled pancake popular as a street food, made from a yeasted wheat dough with milk and filled with brown sugar, honey, chopped peanuts, walnuts or cinnamon. It came from Qing China in the 19th century.
how_to_eat: Eat hot from a paper cup, carefully, as the syrup is very hot.
how_to_order: Buy from street stalls, especially in winter.

name: Dak-galbi
description: Diced chicken stir-fried in gochujang sauce with sweet potato, cabbage, perilla, scallion and rice cakes on a hot plate. Chuncheon dak-galbi is a signature Gangwon dish.
how_to_eat: Wrap pieces in lettuce or perilla leaves, then fry rice in the leftover sauce.
how_to_order: Ask for 'dak-galbi' at restaurants with built-in hot plates in Chuncheon.

name: Mak-guksu
description: Buckwheat noodles served in chilled broth or kimchi soup, sometimes with mustard, sesame oil or vinegar. It is a local specialty of Gangwon, especially Chuncheon.
how_to_eat: Add vinegar and mustard to taste and eat cold.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mak-guksu' at noodle restaurants in Chuncheon.

name: Gamja-ongsimi
description: Chewy grated-potato dumplings boiled in anchovy-kelp broth with zucchini and mushrooms, a type of hand-pulled dough soup. It belongs to Gangwon's simple cuisine based on potato, corn and buckwheat, and is a representative food of Gangneung.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with kimchi.
how_to_order: Ask for 'gamja-ongsimi' at local restaurants in Gangwon, such as in Gangneung.

name: Chodang Sundubu
description: Extra-soft, unpressed tofu from Chodang village in Gangneung, curdled with sea water instead of brine. It is served mild or as spicy sundubu-jjigae stew; its invention is credited to the Joseon official Heo Yeop, though without documentary proof.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and side dishes.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sundubu' at the tofu restaurants of Chodang village in Gangneung.

name: Ojingeo-sundae
description: Whole squid stuffed with a filling of squid legs, beef, tofu, bean sprouts, vegetables and egg, then steamed and sliced. It is a local food of Gangwon and a specialty of Sokcho.
how_to_eat: Eat the slices dipped in chojang (vinegared chilli paste).
how_to_order: Ask for 'ojingeo-sundae' at seafood restaurants on the Gangwon coast.

name: Jeonju Bibimbap
description: Rice cooked in beef shank broth, topped with soybean sprouts, hwangpo-muk (mung bean jelly), gochujang and seasoned raw beef, mixed together before eating. Jeonju is one of the most famous places for bibimbap and holds a yearly bibimbap festival.
how_to_eat: Mix everything thoroughly with the gochujang before eating.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Jeonju bibimbap' at restaurants in Jeonju.

name: Kongnamul-gukbap
description: Rice in soybean sprout soup, seasoned with salted shrimp and topped with scallion and chilli; Jeonju-style is the best-known version. It is often eaten as a hangover cure.
how_to_eat: Mix the rice into the hot soup and add a raw or soft egg if served.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kongnamul-gukbap' at early-opening soup restaurants in Jeonju.

name: Hongeo-hoe
description: Fermented skate with a powerful ammonia smell, a dish from Jeolla province; skate from Heuksando island is the most prized. It is often eaten with pork (bossam) and kimchi as hongeo samhap.
how_to_eat: Eat as 'samhap': a slice of skate with boiled pork and aged kimchi together.
how_to_order: Ask for 'hongeo samhap' at restaurants in Mokpo and South Jeolla.

name: Tteok-galbi
description: Patties of minced beef short rib, originally a royal dish, grilled. Damyang tteok-galbi is the most famous, and a beef-and-pork version was first sold in Gwangju in the 1950s.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and side dishes.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tteok-galbi' at restaurants in Damyang and Gwangju.

name: Ganjang-gejang
description: Raw crabs, mainly females with roe, marinated in soy sauce. Gyeongsang, Jeolla and Jeju are famous for their own types, and it is a representative specialty of Yeosu in South Jeolla.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice, mixing rice into the crab shell.
how_to_order: Ask for 'ganjang-gejang' at seafood restaurants in Jeolla.

name: Makgeolli
description: A milky, lightly sparkling rice wine of about 6-9% alcohol, slightly sweet and tangy. Jeonju is known for makgeolli alleys where kettles of it come with many side dishes.
how_to_eat: Shake or stir gently and drink from a bowl.
how_to_order: Order a kettle at makgeolli houses in Jeonju.

name: Andong Jjimdak
description: Chicken braised with vegetables and glass noodles in a soy sauce-based sauce, spiced with fiery Cheongyang chillies. It originated in the city of Andong, probably in the market's chicken alley.
how_to_eat: Share from a large platter with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'jjimdak' at restaurants in Andong's old market.

name: Heotjesatbap
description: 'Mock ancestral-rite meal': rice with several vegetable namul, mixed with soy sauce instead of gochujang, served with grilled fish and pancakes. Andong is its birthplace.
how_to_eat: Mix the vegetables and soy sauce into the rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'heotjesatbap' at traditional restaurants in Andong.

name: Andong Salted Mackerel
description: Mackerel salted for preservation, then grilled or braised, a local food that originated in inland Andong. Fish carried overland from Yeongdeok was salted on the way, which gave it its seasoning.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Andong godeungeo' at restaurants in Andong.

name: Andong Soju
description: A traditional distilled soju made in Andong, North Gyeongsang.
how_to_eat: Sip neat in small glasses.
how_to_order: Buy at Andong breweries or order at local restaurants.

name: Gwamegi
description: Half-dried Pacific herring or saury, made in winter by freezing and thawing outdoors. It is eaten mostly in North Gyeongsang, with Guryongpo Harbor in Pohang the most famous.
how_to_eat: Wrap in seaweed with green onion and chilli paste.
how_to_order: Ask for 'gwamegi' in Pohang in winter.

name: Makchang-gui
description: Grilled beef abomasum (or pork rectum). It is said to have originated in Daegu.
how_to_eat: Grill at the table and dip in seasoned soybean paste sauce.
how_to_order: Ask for 'makchang' at grill restaurants in Daegu.

name: Agwi-jjim
description: Spicy braised monkfish with soybean sprouts, chilli, doenjang and garlic. It originated at a fish market in Masan and is still a local specialty there.
how_to_eat: Share from the platter with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'agu-jjim' in Masan's Odong-dong district.

name: Hwangnam-ppang
description: A small pastry filled with red bean paste, also called Gyeongju bread. It was first baked in 1939 in Gyeongju's Hwangnam-dong.
how_to_eat: Eat warm with tea.
how_to_order: Buy boxes at bakeries in Gyeongju.

name: Dwaeji-gukbap
description: Pork and rice in bone broth, served with salted shrimp, kimchi, garlic and chillies to add. It began as poverty food during the Korean War and is especially popular in Busan.
how_to_eat: Season with the salted shrimp and mix in the rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'dwaeji-gukbap' at gukbap restaurants in Busan.

name: Milmyeon
description: Wheat noodles in cold meat broth (mul) or spicy gochujang sauce (bibim), a variant of naengmyeon. Northern refugees created it in Busan during the Korean War when buckwheat was scarce.
how_to_eat: Add vinegar and mustard and eat cold.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mul milmyeon' or 'bibim milmyeon' at noodle restaurants in Busan.

name: Busan Eomuk
description: Fish cake skewers simmered in hot broth, sold from street stalls. Korea's eomuk industry grew in Busan after the Korean War.
how_to_eat: Eat from the skewer and sip the broth from a paper cup.
how_to_order: Buy skewers at street stalls and markets in Busan.

name: Dongnae Pajeon
description: A scallion pancake where whole scallions keep their shape, made with a rice-flour, egg and gochujang batter, often with beef and seafood. It is named after Dongnaeeupseong, a Joseon-era fortress now in Busan.
how_to_eat: Dip in soy-vinegar sauce and eat with makgeolli.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Dongnae pajeon' at restaurants in Dongnae, Busan.

name: Ssiat Hotteok
description: Busan-style 'seed hotteok': a sweet pancake with brown sugar filling, stuffed with a variety of seeds. Street vendors cluster near BIFF Square.
how_to_eat: Eat hot from a paper cup.
how_to_order: Buy from street vendors at BIFF Square, Busan; cash is best.

name: Jeju Black Pork
description: Grilled pork from the Jeju Black, a native black pig breed of the island. In Jeju it is eaten dipped in fermented anchovy sauce (meljeot).
how_to_eat: Grill at the table and dip in the anchovy sauce warmed on the grill.
how_to_order: Ask for 'heukdwaeji' at barbecue restaurants on Jeju.

name: Gogi-guksu
description: Pork-based wheat noodle soup served with sliced pork and chives. It developed in the 20th century and is now widely associated with Jeju.
how_to_eat: Eat hot, slurping noodles and broth.
how_to_order: Ask for 'gogi-guksu' at noodle shops in Jeju City.

name: Jeonbok-juk
description: Rice porridge made with abalone, sometimes with its innards for a green tinge. It developed in Jeju, with its haenyeo diving culture, and Gangwon's east coast; seafood porridges are representative main dishes of Jeju cuisine.
how_to_eat: Eat warm, often as breakfast.
how_to_order: Ask for 'jeonbok-juk' at restaurants near Jeju's coast.

name: Jari-mulhoe
description: Raw damselfish (jari) in a cold soup, one of Jeju's raw fish dishes. Raw seafood is a common part of Jeju meals.
how_to_eat: Eat cold, mixing in rice or noodles if served.
how_to_order: Ask for 'jari-mulhoe' at seafood restaurants on Jeju in summer.

name: Omegi-tteok
description: A rice cake particular to Jeju, traditionally made with millet. Today it is one of the island's best-selling souvenir snacks.
how_to_eat: Eat as a snack with tea.
how_to_order: Buy at markets and souvenir shops on Jeju.
